page: Microsoft Azure D48d_v5 is a general-purpose instance powered by the third-generation Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the virtual machine provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores via symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation totals 192 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography capabilities such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 1933 GB of bundled local SSD storage, providing high-throughput local disk space without requiring network-attached block volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable mid-tier performance across raw compute and memory evaluations, with standout strengths in vector- and crypto-intensive operations. Multi-core stress-ng tests achieved 46,630.34, while PassMark compute testing reached 48,327.07, placing overall compute in the middle 50 percent of tested cloud instances. Cryptographic throughput proved exceptional, with PassMark encryption reaching 42,548.75 in the top 25 percent, benefiting directly from VAES instructions. Geekbench image processing also placed in the top quartile at 14,999.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 152.26 GB/sec for large un-cached read blocks and 65.92 GB/sec for write operations, supporting steady data throughput for caching layers such as Redis, which sustained 44.26 million SET operations per second.

The inclusion of 1933 GB of local SSD storage provides significant efficiency for workloads dependent on rapid scratch space, caching, or ephemeral indexing, reducing the necessity and expense of high-IOPS external network disks. Because the server lacks dedicated GPU hardware, it is not configured for heavy machine learning training, though it demonstrates capable small-model text generation speeds reaching 285.96 tokens per second on CPU. The balanced ratio of processing capacity, substantial memory, and integrated storage makes the D48d_v5 effective for enterprise relational databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, container orchestration hosts, and transactional data processing.

It offers 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading, 48 MB of L3 cache, and 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes 1933 GB of local SSD storage, avoiding network storage latency for ephemeral data. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI, which drive top-quartile performance in encryption and image processing tests. Compute and general memory benchmarks consistently place within the middle 50 percent of tested platforms, accompanied by 44.26 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. With no integrated GPU, this instance emphasizes dense CPU execution and fast local scratch capacity, making it a fit for relational databases, enterprise web applications, and continuous integration compilation builds.
